title: Annulus fibrosus
summary: Quasi-static tensile stress-strain curves of human annulus: single lamella along fibres, uniaxial circumferential and axial, and biaxial with circumferential strain held.
simulate: Build each specimen as stated: single lamella strip (fibres along the load), multi-lamella strip, cruciform, or square; lamellae at about +-30 deg to the transverse (circumferential) direction.
Orient the load: along fibres (lamella), circumferential, or axial; biaxial = axial stretch with the circumferential grips (or strain) held.
Grip the ends (bony ends rigid); leave lateral faces free except in biaxial; start from the load-free state after any stated preload.
Load quasi-statically (experiments: 0.0001 /s or slower, 1 mm/min, or equilibrium after stepwise holds) up to the last strain of each curve.
Report nominal stress (force / undeformed cross-section, MPa) against nominal strain (change in length / initial length, %), from a central gauge region where the study used one.

studies.sample: 11 lumbar discs, grade I-II; curves = 4 single lamellae (VLe, VLi, De, Di) of one representative unit
11 circumferential anterior AF strips, grade I-II, 6 spines; curve evaluated from mean fit coefficients
60 anterior AF strips, 10 non-degenerate L1-L3 discs; curves = one representative disc (equilibrium)
5 outer anterior AF cruciform specimens, grade I-II; curves = one typical specimen
outer anterior AF strips, L3-L5; 7 non-degenerate (curves = one representative sample)
Bass 2004 typical specimen, E22=0 biaxial run, digitised from Ghezelbash 2021 Fig 5b,c
16 anterior AF square samples, 13 spines; circ-fixed biaxial curve digitised from Ghezelbash 2021 Fig 7a
60 circumferential multi-layer AF strips (AO, AI, PO, PI; 15 each), L3-L4, 15 spines 26-53 y, grade I-II; curves = one typical grade I disc (28 y)

views.title: Single lamella, along fibres
views.note: Uniaxial tension of one lamella with fibres on the load axis; nominal stress = force / load-free area, nominal strain = stretch - 1 (gauge markers).

views.title: Uniaxial circumferential
views.note: Multi-lamella strip pulled circumferentially (fibres at about +-30 deg to the load), sides free; nominal stress vs nominal strain of the central region.

views.title: Uniaxial axial
views.note: Multi-lamella strip pulled axially (fibres at about +-60 deg to the load), sides free; nominal stress vs nominal strain of the central region.

views.title: Biaxial, circumferential held
views.note: Axial stretch with circumferential grips/strain held; axial and circumferential nominal stress vs axial nominal strain of a central 3x3 mm square.

notes: Definitions follow Ghezelbash et al. 2021 (Acta Biomater submission, SSRN 3677348, Fig 4 caption, p.20): nominal strain = applied displacement / initial length; nominal stress = applied force / initial cross-sectional area (first Piola-Kirchhoff); Ghezelbash et al. 2020 (J Biomech 102:109463, Fig 2, p.4) plots 'Nominal Stress' vs 'Engineering Strain'.

Test modes are those the two papers validated against (2020 Sec 2.2 p.2, Fig 2; 2021 Figs 4, 5, 7): single lamella along fibres, uniaxial circumferential and axial, biaxial. Shear, radial, bone-AF-bone failure, rate, creep/relaxation-time and fatigue data are left out.

Most curves are one representative specimen (n=1); Wagner & Lotz is a mean-coefficient fit (derived). Lagrangian strains E (Bass, O'Connell) were converted to nominal strain as sqrt(1+2E) - 1; stresses are as reported. Elliott & Setton values are equilibrium (end of stepwise holds).
agent_prompt: You are given a constitutive or finite element model of human lumbar annulus fibrosus. For every task in this card, build the specimen of its test mode (single lamella along fibres, circumferential or axial multi-lamella strip, or biaxial cruciform/square with the circumferential direction held), load it quasi-statically, and return the nominal stress (force / undeformed cross-sectional area, MPa) at the task's nominal strain (change in length / initial length, %). For biaxial tasks with output transverse_stress return the circumferential (held-direction) nominal stress. Use one parameter set for all tasks; do not refit per task. Return one JSON object following answer_format: task id -> {output key: value}. Use null for tasks your model cannot simulate. Tasks with the same `curve` id are points of one measured curve (see `curves`): you may answer a whole curve as {curve id: [[x, y], ...]} with x in the curve's x unit; it is read at each point by linear interpolation.
